The SCORE Act (H.R. 4312) claims to protect student-athletes but entrenches NCAA bureaucracy. Sec. 5(c) forces schools paying coaches $250K+ to sponsor 16+ varsity teams—a mandate that locks colleges into bloated athletic programs regardless of student interest or fiscal reality. While Sec. 9(b) bans student fees for athletics at schools with $50M+ media revenue, it ignores the real issue: universities redirecting academic funds to sports empires under "grants-in-aid" loopholes.

The bill’s antitrust shield (Sec. 7) protects cartels from accountability while Sec. 10 steamrolls state laws that actually empower athletes. Transparency? Sec. 9(a) disclosure rules are performative—schools already bury fee allocations in opaque budgets.

This isn’t reform; it’s regulatory capture dressed as progress.

AI’s potential in healthcare is real—but let’s not pretend D.C. bureaucrats are the ones driving innovation. The Health Tech Investment Act (S.1399) proves the swamp’s priorities: Section 2(a)(1) mandates Medicare pay for algorithm-based services using FDA-cleared devices, yet Section 2(b) codifies CMS’s “software as a service” policy that’s ripe for abuse.

We’re talking about Medicare Advantage plans already weaponizing AI to deny claims while taxpayers foot the bill for redundant systems. Innovation thrives when government gets out of the way—not when it layers subscription fees and invoice price mandates on providers.

Heard any hearings about slashing FDA’s 20-year-old regulatory frameworks? Exactly. Priorities.

The RESULTS Act is another band-aid for a bullet wound. While protecting seniors' access to lab testing sounds noble, the real issue is systemic bloat. Medicare already hemorrhages billions through fraud and overpriced contracts—why does Congress keep throwing cash at symptoms instead of curing the disease?

Labs shouldn’t need bailouts if D.C. fixed pricing scams and Big Pharma’s monopoly grip. Cut the middlemen, expose the waste, and let market-driven care thrive.

Until then, every “bipartisan fix” just papers over the same corrupt system.
